title: Semi-integral variants as a diagnostic for ES
connection: The semi-integral Markoff-type framework in arXiv:2411.02629 shares ES F13/F06/F01 and offers a feature-flip comparison with F27: relax positivity/integrality and see which part of the local-global theorem survives.
why: A carefully chosen relaxation can isolate whether ES's hard constraint is positivity, integrality, or global coverage.
first_step: Formulate the ES surface's corresponding semi-integral-point question and check whether any theorem in arXiv:2411.02629 applies after a birational change.
areas: ES variants, function fields & other rings

title: Smith theory / ℤ/2-equivariant topology: fixed points of an involution on a ℤ/2-acyclic certificate complex
connection: Smith theory: an involution on a mod-2 acyclic finite complex has a non-empty mod-2 acyclic fixed set. A simplicial complex on solutions (or near-solutions) that is provably ℤ/2-acyclic, with an involution whose fixed points are certificates, would give existence.
why: It is the topological generalisation of 'odd number of fixed points', more flexible than plain parity because acyclicity can be proved by shellability or discrete Morse theory.
first_step: Define a complex on words of all p′ ≤ p (or on near-certificates) with faces from shared letters; compute mod-2 homology for small p.

title: Discrete Morse reductions
connection: Assign a combinatorial gradient to a bounded certificate complex and collapse redundant regions.
why: A reduced complex might isolate the essential obstructions to moving between certificate families.
first_step: Build a small complex from compatible local moves and test elementary collapses with explicit free-face checks.

title: Squarefree obstruction list for xy+yz+zx
connection: OEIS A055745 is the squarefree subset of integers not represented by xy+yz+zx, sharing F25/F08w/F13 and F04: a concrete finite-looking exceptional set arises within an algebraic family and representation counts are computable.
why: Comparing obstruction types rather than just the overall existence theorem may reveal whether ES failures cluster on squarefree or squareful inputs.
first_step: Compute ES failure counts separately for squarefree n and n with square factors over a modest prime range, and compare the apparent exceptional pattern with A055745's finite-list phenomenon.

title: Catalog: Goldbach for Gaussian integers / number fields (Mitsui)
connection: Goldbach for Gaussian integers / number fields (Mitsui) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: —. Status: almost all. Mechanism: Hecke L-functions.
areas: ES variants, function fields & other rings

title: Bhargava–Gauss composition of x²+4dy² values in Type I
connection: Type I needs f | p² + 4c²d: values of the form X² + 4dY² at (p,c); divisors of represented values are represented by forms in the same genus/class group (composition).
why: Recasts the Type I event as a class-group statement about the ideal above f in the order of discriminant −16d — where Bhargava cubes / composition laws act.
first_step: For hard primes, compute the class-group element of each prime divisor of p²+4c²d and see whether the failure is explained by class-group parity.
refs: Bhargava, Higher composition laws I, Ann. Math. 159 (2004)

title: Kloosterman refinement in the level variable t for Σ_t D_t^−(tp+1)
connection: Kloosterman's refinement made 4-variable forms work by averaging Kloosterman sums over the Farey denominators. The all-level ES count Σ_t D_t^−(tp+1) is a divisor problem whose Fourier expansion in t produces Kloosterman sums (cf. the Type I Heegner/Kuznetsov note).
why: Kuznetsov is already used for the Type I sum; applying it to the level sum at fixed p is the pointwise version.
first_step: Write Σ_{t≤T} D_t^−(tp+1) via additive characters, identify the Kloosterman sums S(m,n;c), and estimate their contribution using Weil + Kuznetsov for fixed p.

title: Explicit Burgess (Treviño) to make the 'BM layer is pointwise free' statement fully explicit
connection: SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9 Prop 2.2: some 4 | t ≤ 4ℓ(p) has a positive BM main term iff p is not a square. Explicit Burgess bounds (Treviño, McGown) give explicit ℓ(p) ≤ p^{1/4√e+ε}-type bounds with constants.
why: It gives an explicit, verifiable statement that is the first layer of ES, for formal verification and for any explicit-range argument.
first_step: Plug Treviño's explicit least-QNR bound into Prop 2.2; state the explicit level bound for all p ≥ 10²⁰.
refs: Treviño, The least quadratic non-residue and related problems (2015; check)

title: Odd-square neighbours in the ES₅ word form: tuv − u − v = m² has no 'interior' words? T1 in word language
connection: ES₅ word certificates should exhibit T1 at squares ↔ word-level proof of T1 might identify an invariant (like a Jacobi symbol of t,u,v) that is constant on words.
why: An invariant constant on words but nonconstant on primes would be a hidden conservation law; T1 says it takes a forbidden value on squares.
first_step: Compute the Jacobi symbol combinations (t/·), (u/v)… on all ES₅ words for small n; look for a combination that equals 1 on all words of non-square n... (check repo first).

title: Feature flip: allow one negative unit fraction — 4/p = 1/((p−1)/4) − 1/(p(p−1)/4) trivially
connection: Positivity (F27) is the whole difficulty: with signs, two terms suffice for p ≡ 1 mod 4. The positive cone is the 'boundary' making the surface log K3-like.
why: Suggests attacking positivity directly: start from the trivial signed solution and move inside the positive cone by symmetries of the cubic surface (Vieta moves / Cremona maps).
first_step: Enumerate signed 3-term solutions with exactly one negative term for hard p and test whether some explicit birational move lands in the positive cone.

title: Chain basis ⇔ representation of the binary lattice [[v,−1],[−1,t]] with a prescribed orthogonal vector
connection: A chain basis exists iff the ternary lattice L contains a primitive binary sublattice ≅ [[v,−1],[−1,t]] whose orthogonal complement direction meets L appropriately. This is a 'representation of binary forms by ternary forms' problem with an extra condition.
why: Representation of binary forms by ternary/quaternary forms has deep equidistribution results (Ellenberg–Venkatesh; Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh). These give existence for large discriminant, but with growing discriminant here.
first_step: Formulate: for each binary form b of disc ≈ 4tv−4 ≤ X, is b represented by a ternary of det p in the non-square genus with the extra e₃ condition? Compare with the Ellenberg–Venkatesh hypotheses.
refs: Ellenberg–Venkatesh, Local-global principles for representations of quadratic forms (Invent. 2008)

title: Hecke operators on the space of words: does T_ℓ map ES₅ words of p to words of ℓp or ℓ²p?
connection: Hecke operators act on SL₂(ℤ)-cosets/matrices with fixed determinant structure. Words are SL₂ matrices with upper-right entry p. Hecke correspondences relate matrices with entry p to entry ℓp.
why: It is the modular-forms-native way to get relations between different n. A Hecke-equivariant structure on certificates would allow induction.
first_step: Apply the coset representatives of T_2 to γ_w and check which images are words (positive, upper-right p or 4p) and how the sign transforms.

title: Catalog: Twin primes / bounded gaps (Zhang, Maynard)
connection: Twin primes / bounded gaps (Zhang, Maynard) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: x/log² x. Obstruction: parity. Status: open; bounded gaps proved. Mechanism: GPY/Maynard sieve.

title: Rotation structure: fixing two word parameters makes ES a progression
connection: BGS's middle game uses 'rotations' (fix one Markoff coordinate → conic with a cyclic action). ES words p = tuv − u − v: fixing (t, u) gives v(tu − 1) = p + u, an arithmetic condition mod tu − 1; fixing (u, v) gives t·uv = p + u + v. Use these one-parameter 'rotations' to move between certificate-bearing and non-bearing configurations.
why: The local-to-global passage in BGS relies on such fibrations; ES has them in elementary form.
first_step: For hard p, compute for each (t,u) with tu ≤ T the residue of p + u mod tu − 1 and visualise the hit structure; look for orbit-like propagation.
refs: arXiv:2011.12940 (Chen, Nonabelian level structures, Nielsen equivalence, and Markoff triples, Ann. Math. 2024)

title: Strictly ordered cubic-form representations and symmetry reduction
connection: OEIS A093669 counts unique representations by ab+ac+bc under 0<a<b<c, removing permutation symmetry. It shares F04/F13/F14: a symmetric three-variable surface whose raw point count is converted to canonical unordered witnesses.
why: ES's S3 symmetry creates overcounting; the ordered-triple convention in this sequence offers an exact and transparent normalization.
first_step: For primes p, count only x≤y≤z ES triples and compare with the fully ordered count, separately tracking repeated-coordinate strata.

title: Skorobogatov–Sofos: Schinzel's Hypothesis on average → ES certificate families
connection: SS prove Schinzel's Hypothesis H for 100% of polynomials in families ordered by coefficient height and deduce Hasse principle for 100% of fibred varieties; ES certificates are values of polynomials in (c,d,e) tied to p.
why: Gives a rigorous 'almost all polynomials in a family behave' statement, the polynomial analogue of 'almost all p'.
first_step: Embed the ES Type I certificate polynomial family into a family indexed by coefficients and check which statement of SS transfers (likely 'ES for 100% of a coefficient family', not ES itself).
refs: Skorobogatov–Sofos, Schinzel Hypothesis on average and rational points, Invent. Math. (2023), arXiv:2005.02998
